transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-10-12
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE); Priya Singh (Redwood SE); Mark Liu (Cascade - Head of Platform); Sofia Ramirez (Cascade - ML Eng); Jordan Park (Cascade - Security/Infra)
---
Summary (auto):
Short discovery focused on integration options for Redwood (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private), SDK/assistant integrations (LangChain/LlamaIndex), gateway/proxy patterns, rate limiting and quotas, and observability hooks. Customer wants a POC to validate latency and integration with their gateway.
Topics: SDKs, LangChain/LlamaIndex connectors, gateway/proxy, rate limits/quotas, observability hooks, security requirements, trial setup.
---
Transcript:
[00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. this is Alex from Redwood, AE on the account, priya our solutions engineer is here too. how's everyone doing?
[00:18] Mark Liu: good, thanks Alex. um, big topic for us is integration surface, we run a custom gateway in front of all model calls, and we need to understand how Redwood fits in — hosted vs dedicated vs private, and how the SDK plays with our stack.
[00:32] Priya Singh: great, thanks Mark. quick agenda: run through your current infra, show integration patterns (SDK, direct API, LangChain/LlamaIndex helpers), discuss rate limits/quotas and observability hooks, and outline next steps for a POC. sound good?
[00:46] Mark Liu: yep.
[00:48] Sofia Ramirez: also curious about how easy it is to swap models in the client, and whether you have prebuilt connectors for LangChain and LlamaIndex — we use both in different microservices.
[01:02] Alex Chen: yeah, we ship SDKs for node/python and have example connectors for LangChain and LlamaIndex. Priya can show the patterns: direct SDK, using our gateway proxy, and embedding caching.
[01:18] Priya Singh: quick context — typical integration is either direct SDK call from app -> Redwood hosted API, or app -> internal gateway/proxy -> Redwood. For Dedicated/Private, you can host a private control plane and route traffic inside your VPC, so the gateway stays internal.
[01:40] Jordan Park: for security, we prefer gateway/proxy pattern because we can enforce egress, mTLS and centralize logging. Any gotchas with that?
[01:50] Priya Singh: not really. customers do a reverse-proxy pattern: your gateway adds auth and telemetry, then forwards to Redwood. For hosted we recommend token rotation and client-side retries; for Dedicated we can peer or set up private link. There are also per-route headers for trace ids so your gateway can correlate requests.
[02:12] Mark Liu: about rate limits — we expect bursty traffic, sometimes 200\u2013300 qps for embeddings, and steady 50 qps for generation. how do quotas and rate limiting work?
[02:25] Alex Chen: we have tenant-level quotas and per-key rate limiting. for Dedicated you can reserve capacity with committed throughput; for hosted you'll hit soft quota, and we can raise limits or set burst policies. also you can configure per-route limits in the console or via API.
[02:40] Sofia Ramirez: is there a local SDK option for offline/on-prem inference? like run a model in our environment but manage from Redwood?
[02:50] Priya Singh: that's our Private deployment model — we ship a control plane+runtime you can deploy in VPC or on-prem. it supports KMS integrations and audit logs. some customers do a hybrid: Dedicated in the cloud for most traffic and Private for regulated data.
[03:05] Mark Liu: ok. about LangChain/LlamaIndex: do you provide maintained connectors or just examples?
[03:14] Priya Singh: we maintain official examples and an adaptor repo; for LangChain we have an LLM wrapper and an embeddings client that plugs into the LLMChain. LlamaIndex examples show document loaders -> embeddings -> index calls. the examples include batching and KV cache usage.
[03:32] Sofia Ramirez: great — do the examples support stream responses and function calling? we rely on streaming for UX.
[03:40] Priya Singh: yes, streaming is supported in SDKs and LangChain wrappers. function/tool calling patterns are in the examples but since transcription might be fuzzy some names are mis-typed in the docs — we'll send a cleaned guide.
[03:55] Jordan Park: monitoring — what observability hooks are available? we need latency per-route, token-level cost, traces, and audit logs.
[04:05] Alex Chen: Console gives per-route token/cost breakdown, traces, and full request logs for Dedicated/Private. For hosted we retain request-level logs for configurable retention windows; enterprise customers can increase retention or forward logs to their SIEM. We also expose Prometheus metrics and tracing hooks (open-telemetry).
[04:26] Mark Liu: ok, and for the gateway pattern will we be able to inject our trace ids and get matching traces in Redwood?
[04:33] Priya Singh: yes, you can pass X-Request-Id or a trace header and it's surfaced in logs for correlation. we also support passing custom metadata fields that show up in the console.
[04:45] Mark Liu: good. about latency — our SLA target is p95 < 350ms for short prompts (<= 256 tokens). do you have benchmarks?
[04:56] Alex Chen: we have model profiles and latency benchmarks — we'll share a short spreadsheet. typical hosted latencies depend on model family and sequence length; Dedicated gets more predictable p95s because of reserved capacity.
[05:10] Sofia Ramirez: if we do a POC, can we run a benchmark from our region to your infra? we want realistic numbers including our gateway overhead.
[05:20] Priya Singh: absolutely. we can provide a runbook — Sofia can run a standard harness that simulates your QPS and sequence length. we suggest running prefix caching and batching options.
[05:33] Mark Liu: anything around SDK rate limit handling — e.g., backoff, jitter, retries — is that built-in?
[05:42] Priya Singh: our SDK includes retry/backoff helpers and an optional client-side token bucket for smoothing bursts. the LangChain wrapper also has a retry middleware.
[05:55] Jordan Park: on the security side, we need SOC2 reports and details on key management. is customer-managed KMS supported for Private?
[06:04] Alex Chen: yes, Private supports customer KMS/HSM; Dedicated has integrations for key management too. we'll attach SOC2 and ISO docs.
[06:12] Sofia Ramirez: about cost — embedding vs generation cost calc — any tooling to estimate per-call cost?
[06:20] Alex Chen: Console exposes token-level cost breakdown and cost projection tools; Redwood Optimize can recommend quantization or batching changes to reduce cost. for POC we can run sample traces and provide estimated monthly run rates.
[06:35] Mark Liu: speaking of Optimize, does it provide automated batch size tuning? we have variable payload sizes which makes a big diff in throughput.
[06:45] Priya Singh: it provides suggestions and a simulated throughput model; it's not fully automatic yet but gives recommended batch sizes and quantization profiles per workload.
[06:54] Alex Chen: quick question — do you have restrictions on outbound connections from your gateway? some customers block public egress, which would push them towards Dedicated/Private.
[07:05] Mark Liu: we do block broad egress; we prefer peered connections or Private deployments. but for initial POC we could open a controlled egress to a sandbox.
[07:16] Priya Singh: that makes sense. for POCs we often create a sandbox org with limited ingress IP allowlist.
[07:25] Sofia Ramirez: on swapping models, how smooth is version pinning in the API? can we test A/B?
[07:33] Alex Chen: model pinning and rollouts are supported; you can create routes that point to different model versions and do canary or A/B rollout with automatic fallback if a variant fails or has regressions.
[07:48] Mark Liu: great. any notes about pre-built clients for our stack? we're primarily python backend and some go microservices.
[07:56] Priya Singh: python and node SDKs are first-class. we also have community-contributed go clients; for go we recommend using our HTTP client with a small wrapper.
[08:07] Jordan Park: about observability hooks again — does OpenTelemetry work out of the box?
[08:13] Priya Singh: yes, we provide OTEL-compatible tracing hooks and exporters. you can push spans with trace ids and see full end-to-end traces.
[08:22] Sofia Ramirez: curious about KV cache mention earlier — does Redwood manage KV cache for streaming generation?
[08:29] Priya Singh: the runtime manages KV cache for ongoing chat sessions; for shared caching between requests you can use prefix caching via the API. it helps on repeated contexts to reduce token usage.
[08:44] Mark Liu: any caveats integrating with LlamaIndex for large vector stores? we host vectors ourselves on pinecone-like service.
[08:51] Priya Singh: LlamaIndex patterns work: you push embeddings to your vector DB and use Redwood embeddings client. we have guidance on batching embeddings and rate limits to avoid DB throttling.
[09:02] Alex Chen: at this point maybe we should outline a POC scope — Sofia to run integration tests using SDK + gateway pattern, one benchmark run for generation and one for embeddings, security review from Jordan, and produce a latency/cost report.
[09:20] Mark Liu: sounds right. timeline wise we'd like a 2\u20133 week POC and decision within a month if numbers look good.
[09:29] Alex Chen: we can do that. Priya will own the runbook and benchmarks, I'll send pricing and the SDK examples.
[09:36] Priya Singh: action items — I'll prepare a benchmark runbook, a sample LangChain/LlamaIndex repo, and examples showing gateway headers and trace correlation.
[09:46] Jordan Park: i'll send the security questionnaire back with network constraints.
[09:52] Sofia Ramirez: i'll assemble a small dataset and expected QPS patterns — i'd like sample code to run locally against the sandbox.
[09:59] Alex Chen: perfect. any competitors you're evaluating?
[10:05] Mark Liu: we're also looking at OpenAI (hosted), Anthropic in some cases, and our internal on-prem solution for compliance-heavy flows.
[10:15] Alex Chen: understood. we'll highlight Dedicated/Private options for restricted egress and compliance.
[10:22] Mark Liu: one final question — are there SDK limits on concurrent streams or socket connections?
[10:28] Priya Singh: limits exist per-org to prevent noisy neighbors; for Dedicated you can have higher concurrency with reserved capacity. we'll document default socket limits and how to request increases.
[10:40] Alex Chen: okay we'll wrap up with next steps and I'll summarize in email.
